newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SKorea 3-yr yields end up despite BOK intervention.
newsitem.headline: SKorea 3-yr yields end up despite BOK intervention.

text.p: Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds closed higher on Monday despite the central bank's supply of 700 billion won into the money market, traders said.
But the money supply by the Bank of Korea through seven-day repurchase agreements helped overnight call rates close lower.
* 3-yr corporates end up at 12.10 vs Saturday's 12.02
* Overnight average call rates end down at 11.4 vs 11.5
Dealers said about 274 billion won worth of new corporate bonds were issued but the market had a tough time absoring the new supply.
They forecast the yields would rise further for the time being with the corporate yields moving in a 12.20-12.25 percent range this week.
Three-month CDs ended flat on the back of stable short-term money situation. Overnight average call rates closed lower as the central bank supplied 700 billion won to banks.
